Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: ONE isolated environmental landmark sprite for Chronoforge Echo, a richly detailed painted pixel-art science-fantasy RPG. Replacement for a crude flat satellite dish. Must read as a salvaged listening dish, not a household bowl.
Subject: an ancient medium-sized parabolic communications antenna, the gull crown. Wide shallow concave segmented weathered bronze and ivory ceramic dish tilted skyward, dark structural ribs, asymmetric bent receiver arm reaching over its center ending in a small unlit copper receiver, mounted on a squat robust swiveling iron-and-stone pedestal. A little age, salt staining, tiny moss traces, exposed bolts, restrained patinated teal in recesses. Distinct readable functional silhouette, no busy extras. Its total standing height is about twice an adult human; dish wider than pedestal. Aged handcrafted lost technology, subtly fantasy, practical and convincing.
Style: highly detailed painterly pixel-art environmental sprite, crisp tiny pixel contours and textured clustered shading, rich worn material detail, warm upper-left light. Matching detailed overgrown limestone ruins and teal/copper machinery in a top-down 2.5D RPG. No flat vector shapes, no simplistic icon, no smooth plastic 3D model.
Composition: full complete object, slightly elevated three-quarter front view looking down about 25 degrees, near-orthographic game camera. Entire receiver and complete pedestal foot visible. Centered inside a square canvas with 10% clear margin on every side. Compact organic footprint, no terrain tile, no square ground plinth. No cast shadow, no people, no text, no UI, no frame, no logo. ONE sprite only, not a sheet.
Background: genuinely TRANSPARENT RGBA background around and through all gaps in the structure. Do not paint any checkerboard or opaque backdrop; preserve generated alpha.

Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: ONE isolated covered expedition caravan wagon environmental sprite for Chronoforge Echo, a richly detailed painted pixel-art science-fantasy RPG.
Subject: a sturdy traveling shelter built on a weathered timber wagon with four large clearly visible iron-rimmed wooden spoked wheels, two foremost wheels especially readable. Tall arched muted dark teal canvas cover over curved wooden ribs, slightly patched, warm brown plank lower body, a small rear step and door facing partly toward camera, strapped rolled blankets and two small travel trunks, aged copper corner brackets, one small unlit hanging lantern. No draft animals, no person, no chimney or stone house. A mobile survivor's camp usable beside desert or snowy roads. Elegant worn handcraft, compact convincing wheel-to-body joins. All wheel bottoms intact.
Style: highly detailed painted pixel-art environmental sprite, crisp tiny stepped pixel edges and rich textured shading. Materials visibly wood, canvas, aged iron and copper. Warm upper-left light. Matches a 2.5D top-down fantasy RPG with detailed limestone ruins, desert mudbrick buildings, teal cloth and salvage technology. No flat vector shapes, no icon style, no smooth plastic 3D toy.
Composition: full complete vehicle in elevated three-quarter view looking down about 25 degrees, near-orthographic game camera. Broad rear and one long side visible. Overall silhouette slightly wider than tall, visually one coherent prop. Centered square canvas, 10% clear transparent margin all around. NO ground patch or terrain, no background scenery, no cast shadow, no text, no UI, no border, no watermark. ONE sprite only, not a sprite sheet.
Background: genuinely TRANSPARENT RGBA exterior including the gaps beneath wagon and between spokes; preserve alpha, do not paint a checkerboard or opaque backdrop.

processing: Original 1254×1254 RGBA PNGs copied byte-for-byte; rendering crops transparent outer margins only. No repainting, background keying, resizing or alpha alteration.
